output:
I ran `infrastructure-fit` in Review mode. One thing to state up front: this working directory contains only the skill library and `CLAUDE.md` — no product code, no git history. So every signal below is as you reported it, not verified by me from source. §7 step 1 ("inventory from the source of truth") did not run.

## What I found

Your document database is `INHERITED` — a template default nobody decided, which the skill treats as not a decision at all. The verdict is **switch it, and do it now before customers arrive (the record calls this MIGRATE)**. What decides it: four of the six signals in the §6 "relational domain on a non-relational store" row fired at once — hand-written uniqueness checks, conflict retries, joins in application code, readers for old document shapes — and your scale ceiling (tens of small customers) is nowhere near the only conditions that justify deviating from the one-relational-database default. The three profile dimensions that decide data-model paradigm (domain shape, access patterns, scale) are all filled and all point the same way. Serverless compute and platform sign-in get **KEEP**: no tripwire you reported touches them, so don't bundle them into this migration.

## Why it matters

Acting now costs you a persistence-layer rewrite and a feature stall, against a reversal cost that is at its lifetime minimum: zero real rows, so no backfill, no dual-write, no expand/contract staging — a straight cutover. Not acting means continuing to pay ~1 commit in 8 on store workarounds, and keeping hand-written uniqueness checks that a relational constraint would make atomic — those checks are a correctness risk the moment two writes race, not just a tax. Every customer you onboard first raises the reversal cost.

The one place I'd slow you down: region, tenancy model, and retention are also one-way doors, and they're currently undecided. Provision a new store before closing those and you open a second door as badly as the first.

## Do this first

1. Run the `requirements-grounding` quality sweep on the four blank dimensions — isolation/residency, data lifecycle, cost envelope, lock-in tolerance. Half a day. It decides region and tenancy, which you are about to pick whether or not you look.
2. Write the store record (forcing requirement, rejected alternatives, tripwires, reversal cost) where `zero-copy-requirements` puts decisions, then run the §5 walking skeleton on the new store — including the serverless connection model and a cross-tenant read refusal — before migrating any feature.
3. Cut over, then delete the workaround code: uniqueness checks, conflict retries, application joins, old-shape readers.

## What I did not check

- Whether the reported signals exist in your code: `git log --oneline -- <store paths> | wc -l` against total commits, and a grep for the uniqueness/retry/join sites. I counted nothing.
- Whether your platform sign-in shares a vendor with the document database (common in starters). `grep -rE 'firebase|amplify|cognito|supabase' <config>` — if it does, your erasure path will span two vendors after the switch.
- Whether your serverless runtime can hold relational connections at your request rate. The skeleton closes this.
- Pricing at zero load on both candidates. No cost envelope exists to check against.

---

```text
Mode:            Review (first real data about to enter; multiple §6 tripwires reported)
Component:       Document database (primary store)
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED — no record of why it was chosen
Forcing need:    None found. Template default.
Profile:         Domain shape: relational — employers, employees, roles, assessments,
                 reports joining them; cross-entity uniqueness and referential
                 integrity; multi-entity writes implied by conflict retries.
                 Access patterns: joins and joining reports (hardest 3 not enumerated).
                 Scale: tens of small customers, ceiling stated.
                 GAP: isolation/residency, data lifecycle, cost, lock-in tolerance.
Evidence:        REPORTED, NOT VERIFIED — hand-written uniqueness checks, write-conflict
                 retries, application-code joins, old-document-shape readers (4 of 6
                 signals in the relational-mismatch row); ~1 commit in 8 touches the
                 store (platform-tax row). No skeleton has been run on any candidate.
Verdict:         MIGRATE
Justification:   Forward costs only. Staying: ongoing ~12.5% commit share on store
                 workarounds, non-atomic uniqueness enforcement, growing old-shape
                 reader surface. Migrating: persistence rewrite at zero real rows —
                 no backfill, no dual-write, no staged contract. Scale ceiling excludes
                 every §3 condition for deviating from one relational database.
                 Sunk six months is not an argument.
Tripwires:       Post-migration — any hand-written cross-entity integrity check reaching
                 review (threshold: 1); store-touching commit share >5% per month.
                 Owner: tech lead. Evaluated: PR review and monthly review.
Reversal cost:   Low today. Rises with the first customer's rows, and again with each
                 tenant whose data cannot be truncated.
Handoff:         requirements-grounding (close 4 GAP dimensions, before provisioning);
                 then evolutionary-database-design (cutover, which with no real data
                 is a replace, not an expand/contract);
                 then structural-simplification (count the D/K delta from deleting
                 the workaround layer)
Next action:     Run the grounding sweep on residency, retention, cost, lock-in.
```

```text
Mode:            Review (same trigger)
Component:       Serverless backend (compute and hosting)
Door:            ONE-WAY
Status:          INHERITED → PROVISIONAL (operability, workload shape, cost are GAP)
Forcing need:    None found. Template default. Plausibly fits: idle-heavy load at
                 tens of small customers is where scale-to-zero pays.
Profile:         Scale: tens of small customers. Workload shape: GAP (batch imports,
                 schedules, report generation unclassified). Operability: GAP (team
                 size, on-call). Cost: GAP (no envelope, idle or loaded).
Evidence:        NOT VERIFIED. No reported platform-glue incident, parity gap, or
                 cold-start complaint. The store tripwires implicate the store, not
                 compute.
Verdict:         KEEP
Tripwires:       Connection exhaustion or pooler latency against the new relational
                 store (threshold: any error at expected peak in the skeleton);
                 report generation exceeding the function execution limit.
                 Owner: tech lead. Evaluated: skeleton run, then release gate.
Reversal cost:   Moderate and roughly flat; unaffected by customer data volume.
Handoff:         None. Re-enters Review if a tripwire fires or the GAP dimensions
                 move it.
Next action:     Add the relational connection model to the §5 skeleton. Change nothing
                 else about compute during the store migration — one one-way door
                 at a time.
```

```text

Component:       Platform-managed sign-in (identity provider and user store)
Door:            ONE-WAY

Forcing need:    None found. Template default, but matches the §3 default
                 (standards-based provider; application owns authorization).
Profile:         Identity: employer and employee sign-in, administrative roles

Verdict:         KEEP
Tripwires:       A customer requiring SSO or federation the provider cannot meet;
                 authorization logic migrating into provider-proprietary claims
                 (threshold: 1 occurrence). Owner: tech lead. Evaluated: periodic review.
Reversal cost:   High and rises with every registered account — higher than the
                 store's, which is why it must not be swept into this migration.
Handoff:         None.
Next action:     Confirm whether sign-in and the document store share a vendor. If so,

```
